findings: The real original R/scripts/std_mir_source_paths.py is loaded under a private name; __file__ and ROOT remain original R. Its unchanged main imports runtime_compiler while std_cli.invoke holds the authenticated new runtime alias.

The supervisor keeps the same public alias context across supervised, so original std lazy imports and post-child std.load use the declared original modules with the selected new runtime. Neither route copies the original std module to a new ROOT.

The new runtime load_runtime_compiler reconstructs identity using its optional validated loader_probe policy; the original implementation would not provide this new semantic key. Both wrapper and ordinary CLI select the same new source.

Audit12 phase_result supplies runtime_key/sysroot/ready_sha256/admission_sha256/qualification_sha256 and the four false downstream-scope flags exactly as runtime_proof consumes. Top-level saved_audit_source, receipt_sha256 and finished_at are produced by audit12.

The initial ready.identity.admission == admission.json mismatch is corrected: prefix admission.json is exact {identity,snapshots}; publication_identity now compares full typed ready.identity to admission.identity. The original specification remains nested under identity.admission.
Terminal receipt association uses existing phase/status/key/sysroot plus externally audited receipt SHA; it does not invent terminal owner/work fields.
The single typed source-freeze placeholder avoids putting its own digest into the frozen plan; validate_plan restricts the exact command shape before expansion.
